categories.main_business_segments: Chevron operates two primary business segments: Upstream and Downstream. The Upstream segment focuses on the exploration, development, production, and transportation of crude oil and natural gas, as well as liquefied natural gas (LNG) activities. The Downstream segment is engaged in refining crude oil, marketing petroleum products and lubricants, manufacturing and marketing renewable fuels, and producing petrochemicals and additives. Additionally, Chevron has interests in chemicals (via Chevron Phillips Chemical Company), pipelines, shipping, and new energies initiatives.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Chevron utilizes advanced exploration and production technologies, including horizontal drilling, hydraulic fracturing, and enhanced oil recovery. In refining, the company employs proprietary processes such as ISOALKY™ for alkylation and co-processing of bio-feedstocks for renewable fuels. The company also invests in carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS), digital transformation, and R&D for lower carbon solutions, including hydrogen and renewable base oils.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Chevron serves a broad range of customers including industrial, commercial, and retail consumers. Key markets include transportation (fuels and lubricants), power generation (natural gas), chemicals and plastics manufacturers, and aviation (jet fuel). The company supplies products through branded service stations (Chevron, Texaco, Caltex), direct commercial sales, and wholesale channels worldwide.
categories.geographic_coverage: Chevron operates globally with significant activities in North America (notably the U.S. Permian Basin and Gulf of Mexico), South America (Argentina, Brazil, Canada), Africa (Angola, Nigeria, Republic of Congo), Asia (Bangladesh, China, Indonesia, Israel, Kazakhstan, Thailand), Australia (Gorgon and Wheatstone LNG), and Europe (UK). The company’s operations span over 180 countries, with major assets and projects on six continents.
categories.supply_chain_position: Chevron is an integrated energy company operating across the entire oil and gas value chain. It is active upstream (exploration and production), midstream (pipelines, LNG, shipping), and downstream (refining, marketing, chemicals). The company also participates in renewable energy and new energy value chains, including RNG, hydrogen, and carbon offsets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Chevron’s strategic focus is on delivering higher returns, lowering carbon intensity, and providing superior shareholder value. The company is investing in lower carbon businesses such as renewable fuels, hydrogen, and CCUS, targeting hard-to-abate sectors. R&D priorities include digital transformation, advanced materials, process optimization, and breakthrough technologies for energy transition. Chevron has committed $10 billion through 2028 for lower carbon investments.
categories.revenue_model: Chevron generates revenue primarily through the sale of crude oil, natural gas, refined petroleum products, chemicals, and lubricants. Additional revenue streams include marketing and retail sales, equity income from affiliates, pipeline and shipping services, and licensing of proprietary technologies. The company also earns from renewable fuels and emerging energy solutions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Chevron competes with major integrated oil companies (such as ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, and TotalEnergies), national oil companies, and independent producers in both upstream and downstream sectors. In chemicals, it competes with global petrochemical firms. Chevron is positioned as one of the world’s largest publicly traded energy companies, with a strong presence in both traditional and lower carbon energy markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2021, Chevron reported $155.6 billion in sales and other operating revenues and net income of $15.6 billion, rebounding from a loss in 2020. The company produced a record 3.1 million barrels of oil-equivalent per day and had total assets of $239.5 billion at year-end. Chevron maintains a strong balance sheet, investment-grade credit ratings, and a history of stable dividends, with a focus on disciplined capital allocation and moderate growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Chevron emphasizes reliable, affordable, and ever-cleaner energy solutions, leveraging its integrated operations, global scale, and technological expertise. The company differentiates itself through operational efficiency, a strong safety and environmental record, and a growing portfolio of lower carbon products. Chevron’s value proposition includes a commitment to shareholder returns, innovation, and leadership in the energy transition.
